ranked_facts.concept_key: negative results for hiv and other autoantibodies
ranked_facts.why: The absence of HIV and other autoantibodies makes B4 less likely, while B1 remains a possible diagnosis due to the presence of other autoantibodies.
Normal coagulation parameters are more consistent with B2, which involves interstitial lung disease, whereas B3, which involves vasculitis, might be expected to have abnormal coagulation parameters.
